mainTopic: The dowry dispute between אדמון and the חכמים, when the הלכה follows אדמון, and whether signing as a witness on a field's sale cancels one's own claim to it.
overview: The amud opens with the end of a משנה. A father promised his future son-in-law a dowry and could not pay. The חכמים say the bride waits unmarried, while אדמון says she can demand 'marry me or release me,' and רבן גמליאל agrees with אדמון. A ברייתא of רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says everyone agrees when the father promised, and the real dispute is when the bride promised the money herself. Another ברייתא adds that with a קטנה the court forces someone, and רבא explains that this means forcing the groom to give a גט. Next, רבי יצחק בן אלעזר rules that wherever רבן גמליאל says 'I see the words of אדמון,' the הלכה follows אדמון, even in a ברייתא. The גמרא then tests several readings of רבי זירא's statement about חנן and אדמון. It concludes that only the rulings of אדמון that רבן גמליאל endorsed are the הלכה. Finally, a new משנה discusses a man who claims a field even though he signed as a witness on its sale, and אביי limits the loss of his claim to a witness, not a judge.

steps.title: The משנה's dispute: must the bride wait, or can she demand a decision?
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים say the bride must wait unmarried. אדמון says she can tell the groom: marry me or release me.
steps.simpleTranslation: The bride may sit unmarried until her hair turns white. אדמון says she can argue: 'If I had promised the money myself, I would accept waiting until my hair turns white. But my father made the promise, so what can I do? Either marry me or release me.'
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה finishes a dispute about a father who promised money to his son-in-law and then went broke. The חכמים say the groom does not have to marry her, so she just waits, but אדמון says she can force him to choose.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The חכמים hold that the groom agreed to the marriage on the condition of the money, so if it never comes, he cannot be forced to marry. אדמון's point is that the bride did nothing wrong, since it was her father who made the promise. So it is unfair to leave her stuck: the groom must either marry her or give her a גט.

keyTerms.meaning: She will sit until her head turns white, meaning she stays unmarried indefinitely
Committed or promised a set amount of money, usually for a dowry
Either marry (bring her in) or release her with a גט
A judge in ירושלים whose rulings appear in this פרק

phrases.english: She may sit until her head turns white.
phrases.notes: This is the view of the חכמים. The father promised a dowry and went broke, so the groom can't be forced to marry her.

phrases.english: Admon says: She can say:
Had I promised the money for myself,
I would sit until my head turns white;
now that Father is the one who promised,
what can I do?
Either marry me, or release me.
phrases.notes: 'Release' means giving her a גט so she is free to marry someone else.

steps.mimraCoreRuling: The חכמים say the bride waits indefinitely. אדמון says that since her father made the promise, she can demand that the groom marry her or divorce her.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל sides with אדמון
steps.stepSummary: רבן גמליאל says he agrees with אדמון's position.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבן גמליאל said: I see the words of אדמון as correct.
steps.whatsHappening: רבן גמליאל closes the משנה by agreeing with אדמון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This adds the weight of the נשיא to אדמון's view. The bride is not left stuck, and the groom must either marry her or give a גט.

keyTerms.meaning: I see the words of, meaning I agree with this opinion

phrases.english: Rabban Gamliel said:
I see the words of Admon as correct.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל: רוֹאֶה אֲנִי אֶת דִּבְרֵי אַדְמוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives רבן גמליאל's agreement with אדמון's view from step 1.

steps.title: A ברייתא says there is no dispute when the father promised
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא says our משנה does not follow רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה. He holds that everyone agrees with אדמון when the father promised the money and went broke.
steps.simpleTranslation: Our משנה does not follow this תנא. As it was taught: רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה said: אדמון and the חכמים did not disagree about a man who promised money to his son-in-law and then went broke. In that case everyone agrees she can say, 'My father promised for me, what can I do?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a ברייתא that describes the dispute differently from our משנה. According to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, in the case of the משנה (the father promised), even the חכמים agree with אדמון.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In our משנה, the father's promise is exactly where they argue. רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה says that case is not argued at all: the bride clearly is not to blame, so everyone lets her demand marriage or a גט. This means the real argument must be somewhere else, and the next step will say where.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה does not follow this תנא's view
Literally 'stretched out the leg,' meaning he went bankrupt
They did not disagree

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix up the two versions. In our משנה, the father's promise is the case they argue about. In the ברייתא, the father's promise is agreed by everyone, and the argument is about the bride's own promise.

phrases.aramaic: גְּמָ׳ מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כִּי הַאי תַּנָּא,
phrases.english: GEMARA: Our mishna is not in accordance with this tanna,

phrases.aramaic: דְּתַנְיָא: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹסֵי בְּרַבִּי יְהוּדָה:
phrases.english: as it was taught: Rabbi Yosei, son of Rabbi Yehuda, said:
Admon and the Rabbis did not disagree
about one who promises money to his son-in-law
and then went bankrupt,
that she can say:

phrases.aramaic: ״אַבָּא פָּסַק עָלַי, מָה אֲנִי יְכוֹלָה לַעֲשׂוֹת״.
phrases.english: "Father promised for me; what can I do?"

steps.triggerLanguage: מַתְנִיתִין דְּלָא כִּי הַאי תַּנָּא, דְּתַנְיָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows that a ברייתא places the dispute of the משנה in a different case.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to רבי יוסי ברבי יהודה, when the father promised and went broke, everyone agrees the bride can demand marriage or a גט.

steps.title: Where they really argue: the bride promised the money herself
steps.stepSummary: The ברייתא says the dispute is when the bride herself promised the money. The חכמים say she waits, and אדמון says she can claim she was relying on her father. רבן גמליאל agrees with אדמון.
steps.simpleTranslation: About what did they disagree? About a case where she promised the money herself. The חכמים say she sits until her hair turns white. אדמון says she can argue: 'I thought my father would pay for me. Now that he is not paying, what can I do? Either marry me or release me.' רבן גמליאל said: I see the words of אדמון as correct.
steps.whatsHappening: The ברייתא continues and identifies the case they actually argue about: the bride made the promise herself. It also repeats רבן גמליאל's agreement, now applied to this case.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the חכמים have a stronger point, because she made the promise and did not keep it. אדמון answers that she never had money of her own and was plainly counting on her father. So she is still not really at fault, and the groom must marry her or divorce her.

keyTerms.meaning: She herself promised the money
I thought, or I assumed
Gives on my behalf, pays for me

steps.whatToRemember: According to the ברייתא: when the father promised, everyone agrees with אדמון. When the bride promised herself, the חכמים say she waits, and אדמון (supported by רבן גמליאל) says she can demand marriage or a גט.

phrases.english: About what did they disagree?
About where she promised the money for herself.
For the Rabbis say:
Let her sit until her head turns white.
Admon says: She can say:
I thought that Father would give it for me,
and now that Father is not giving it for me,
what can I do?
Either marry me or release me.
Rabban Gamliel said:
I see the words of Admon as correct.
phrases.notes: Same words as the משנה, but in this ברייתא he is agreeing about the case where she made the promise herself.

steps.triggerLanguage: עַל מָה נֶחְלְקוּ — עַל שֶׁפָּסְקָה הִיא עַל עַצְמָהּ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the ברייתא from step 3 by naming the case that is actually disputed.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When the bride promised herself, the חכמים say she waits indefinitely. אדמון says she can demand marriage or a גט, and רבן גמליאל agrees.

steps.title: Another ברייתא: this applies to a גדולה, but for a קטנה they force
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא limits the ruling to a grown woman. With a young girl, the court 'forces,' without saying whom.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: When is this said? With a גדולה. But with a קטנה, they force.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings another ברייתא that limits the ruling to a grown woman and says that with a young girl the court forces someone. This sets up the question in the next step: force whom?
steps.deeperAnalysis: Leaving the bride to wait applies only to a גדולה, whose own promise counts legally. For a קטנה, the court steps in. The ברייתא does not say whom it forces, and that gap drives the rest of the passage.

keyTerms.meaning: In what case are these words said? A phrase that introduces a limit on a ruling
A grown woman, an adult
A young girl, a minor
The court forces or compels

phrases.english: It was taught: In what case are these words said?
phrases.notes: This refers to the ruling that she sits and waits.

phrases.english: With an adult woman;
but with a minor girl, they compel.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a limit to the ruling that the bride must wait.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Waiting applies to a גדולה. With a קטנה, the court compels someone.

steps.title: Whom does the court force?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks who is being forced in the case of a קטנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They force whom?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a clarifying question about the ברייתא: whom does the court force?
steps.deeperAnalysis: There are two possible people: the father, who could be forced to pay, or the groom, who could be forced to act. The גמרא needs to figure out which one is meant.

keyTerms.meaning: Whom? To whom?

phrases.english: Whom do they compel?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the missing detail in the ברייתא of step 5.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Who is compelled in the case of a קטנה: the father or the groom?

steps.title: It can't mean the father: then it should be the other way around
steps.stepSummary: If the ברייתא meant forcing the father to pay, it would make more sense for the גדולה, not the קטנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say they force the father, it should have said the opposite!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries reading the ברייתא as forcing the father to pay and immediately shows that this reading does not work.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A grown woman's promise counts legally, so if anyone could be held to pay, it would be connected to her case. A young girl's promise has no legal force at all, so it makes no sense to force the father to pay specifically in her case. That would flip the logic, so the father cannot be the one forced.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say, a phrase that introduces a suggestion about to be rejected
It should have said the opposite

phrases.english: If you say the father,
it should have said the opposite!
phrases.notes: He means: forcing the father would fit the adult case better, since a young girl's promise doesn't count anyway.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Tests one possible answer to the question in step 6 and knocks it down.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading that the court forces the father in the case of a קטנה
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Forcing the father to pay would make more sense for a גדולה, whose promise counts, than for a קטנה, whose promise means nothing. So the ברייתא should have said the reverse.

steps.title: רבא: the court forces the groom to give a גט
steps.stepSummary: רבא explains that with a קטנה, the court forces the groom to give her a גט.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, רבא said: They force the husband to give a גט.
steps.whatsHappening: רבא answers the question: the one forced is the groom. He must give the young girl a גט, or else marry her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Since a קטנה's promise has no legal value, she is not held to it and cannot be left stuck waiting. So the court presses the groom: if he will not marry her without the money, he must free her with a גט. This fits the ברייתא without flipping its logic.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather, which introduces the correct explanation after a rejected one
Husband, here the betrothed groom
To give a bill of divorce

steps.whatToRemember: With a גדולה who promised herself, the חכמים say she waits. With a קטנה, the court forces the groom to give a גט (or marry her), because her promise was never legally binding.

phrases.english: Rather, Rava said:
They compel the husband to give a bill of divorce.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶלָּא אָמַר רָבָא: כּוֹפִין לַבַּעַל לִיתֵּן גֵּט
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the correct answer after step 7 ruled out the father.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reinterprets the unnamed subject of 'כופין' as the groom rather than the father
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The court forces the father to pay the dowry.
steps.terutzMaskana: The court forces the groom to give a גט to a קטנה whose promised money was not paid.

steps.title: When רבן גמליאל agrees with אדמון, the הלכה follows אדמון
steps.stepSummary: רבי יצחק בן אלעזר, quoting חזקיה, gives a general rule: wherever רבן גמליאל says 'I see the words of אדמון,' the הלכה follows אדמון.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יצחק בן אלעזר said in the name of חזקיה: Anywhere that רבן גמליאל said, 'I see the words of אדמון,' the הלכה is like him.
steps.whatsHappening: Right after the case where רבן גמליאל agreed with אדמון, the גמרא brings a general rule about how to rule in such cases.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Usually when one person argues against the חכמים, we might expect the הלכה to follow the majority. This rule says that when רבן גמליאל openly backs אדמון, that tips the scale, and we rule like אדמון.

keyTerms.meaning: 'I see the words of,' meaning 'I agree with' someone's opinion
The practical law follows his opinion
Anywhere, in every case
In the name of, quoting someone

steps.whyThisMatters: This rule is the anchor for the whole section. The later reading of רבי זירא's statement will be tested against it.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּחִזְקִיָּה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Yitzchak ben Elazar said in the name of Chizkiya:
Anywhere that Rabban Gamliel said
"I see the words of Admon"
phrases.notes: In other words, 'I agree with אדמון,' just like רבן גמליאל said in the bride case we just learned.

phrases.english: the halacha is like him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּחִזְקִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from the specific bride case, where רבן גמליאל agreed with אדמון, to a general ruling principle.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Wherever רבן גמליאל says he agrees with אדמון, the הלכה follows אדמון.

steps.title: Does the rule apply to a ברייתא too
steps.stepSummary: רבא asks רב נחמן whether this rule also applies when the disagreement appears in a ברייתא and not in the משנה.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבא said to רב נחמן: Does this apply even in a ברייתא?
steps.whatsHappening: רבא asks how far the rule reaches. Does it cover only cases in the משנה, or also cases recorded in a ברייתא, like the bride case from Step 4?
steps.deeperAnalysis: The question matters here because the bride case where רבן גמליאל agreed with אדמון came from a ברייתא. A rule about the הלכה might seem meant only for the משנה, which carries more authority.

keyTerms.meaning: A teaching from the time of the משנה that was not included in the משנה itself
Even

phrases.english: Rava said to Rav Nachman:
Even in a baraita?

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ רָבָא לְרַב נַחְמָן: אֲפִילּוּ בְּבָרַיְיתָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about the scope of the rule just stated.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Does the rule 'הלכה like אדמון when רבן גמליאל agrees' also apply when the dispute is recorded in a ברייתא?

steps.title: Yes, the rule says 'anywhere'
steps.stepSummary: רב נחמן answers that the rule was not limited to the משנה. It says 'anywhere רבן גמליאל said,' so it includes a ברייתא.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Did we say 'in the משנה'?! We said 'anywhere that רבן גמליאל said.'
steps.whatsHappening: רב נחמן answers רבא by pointing to the exact wording of the rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule does not say 'in the משנה'. It says 'anywhere,' so it covers every place where רבן גמליאל agrees with אדמון, including a ברייתא. That means the bride case from Step 4 also follows אדמון.

keyTerms.meaning: Did we say...? (a pushback question meaning 'that's not what we said')
The main text compiled by רבי יהודה הנשיא

steps.whatToRemember: The rule 'הלכה like אדמון when רבן גמליאל agrees' applies everywhere, in a משנה or in a ברייתא.

phrases.english: He said to him:
Did we say "in the Mishna"?!

phrases.aramaic: בְּכׇל מָקוֹם שֶׁאָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל קָאָמְרִינַן.
phrases.english: We said "anywhere that Rabban Gamliel said."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers רבא's question directly.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Yes. The rule says 'anywhere,' so it includes a ברייתא.

steps.title: רבי זירא on the rulings of חנן and אדמון
steps.stepSummary: רבי זירא, quoting רבה בר ירמיה, says: for the two rulings of חנן, the הלכה follows the one who agrees with him; for the seven rulings of אדמון, the הלכה does not follow the one who agrees with him.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי זירא said in the name of רבה בר ירמיה: The two things that חנן said, the הלכה is like the one who agrees with him. The seven things that אדמון said, the הלכה is not like the one who agrees with him.
steps.whatsHappening: A new statement about how to rule on the opinions of חנן and אדמון, the two judges whose rulings appear in this פרק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: For חנן, the 'one who agrees with him' is רבן יוחנן בן זכאי. For אדמון it is רבן גמליאל. The wording is short and unclear, so the גמרא will soon ask what it means.

keyTerms.meaning: Like the one who is similar to him, meaning the one who agreed with his view
One of the judges in ירושלים whose two rulings appear in this פרק
Another judge of ירושלים, who gave seven rulings
Two things, here meaning two rulings

steps.confusionAlert: 'כיוצא בו' does not mean 'like him'. It means 'like the one who is like him', the רבי who agreed with him.

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר יִרְמְיָה:
phrases.english: Rabbi Zeira said that Rabba bar Yirmeya said:
The two things that Chanan said
the halacha is like the one who is similar to him,
phrases.notes: For חנן, that is רבן יוחנן בן זכאי, who said in the משנה that חנן spoke well.

phrases.english: the seven things that Admon said
the halacha is not like the one who is similar to him.
phrases.notes: Here the 'one similar to him' is רבן גמליאל, who agreed with אדמון.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי זֵירָא אָמַר רַבָּה בַּר יִרְמְיָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Brings a second ruling principle about אדמון, which now has to fit with the rule from Step 9.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The two rulings of חנן: הלכה like the one who agrees with him. The seven rulings of אדמון: no הלכה like the one who agrees with him (the גמרא works out what this means in Steps 13–18).

steps.title: What does רבי זירא mean
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבי זירא's statement actually means.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is he saying?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops to ask what this unclear statement means. This sets up the next two steps, where the גמרא tries two readings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'אין הלכה כיוצא בו' about אדמון can be read more than one way. They could mean we never rule like אדמון, or something else. The גמרא needs to pin down the meaning.

keyTerms.meaning: What is he saying? (asking for the meaning of a statement)

phrases.english: What is he saying?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of רבי זירא's statement.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does 'אין הלכה כיוצא בו' about אדמון's seven rulings actually mean?

steps.title: First reading clashes with the rule about רבן גמליאל
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא suggests reading it as 'never like אדמון nor like the one who agrees with him,' but rejects this because רבי יצחק בן אלעזר said the הלכה follows אדמון when רבן גמליאל agrees.
steps.simpleTranslation: If you say this is what he means: For the two rulings of חנן, the הלכה is like him and like the one who agrees with him; and for the seven rulings of אדמון, the הלכה is not like him and not like the one who agrees with him. But didn't רבי יצחק בן אלעזר say in the name of חזקיה: Anywhere that רבן גמליאל said 'I see the words of אדמון,' the הלכה is like him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tries a first reading of רבי זירא and then knocks it down right away.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first reading says we never rule like אדמון, even where רבן גמליאל agrees with him. That directly contradicts the rule from Step 9, which says we do rule like אדמון when רבן גמליאל agrees. So this reading cannot be right.

keyTerms.meaning: If you say (introduces a suggestion the גמרא is about to reject)
This is what he means
But didn't (someone) say...? (introduces a contradiction)

phrases.english: If you say this is what he means:
The two things that Chanan said
the halacha is like him and like the one who is similar to him,
and the seven things that Admon said

phrases.aramaic: — אֵין הֲלָכָה כְּמוֹתוֹ וְלֹא כַּיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ.
phrases.english: the halacha is not like him and not like the one who is similar to him.

phrases.aramaic: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּחִזְקִיָּה:
phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yitzchak ben Elazar say in the name of Chizkiya:
Anywhere that Rabban Gamliel said

phrases.aramaic: ״רוֹאֶה אֲנִי אֶת דִּבְרֵי אַדְמוֹן״ — הֲלָכָה כְּמוֹתוֹ!
phrases.english: "I see the words of Admon," the halacha is like him!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Offers a first reading of רבי זירא and shows it contradicts Step 9.
steps.kashyaTarget: The reading of רבי זירא that we never rule like אדמון at all.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יצחק בן אלעזר ruled that the הלכה follows אדמון whenever רבן גמליאל agrees. A reading that says never follow אדמון contradicts that.

steps.title: Correct reading: the הלכה follows אדמון in all seven
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads רבי זירא: for אדמון, the הלכה is not just like רבן גמליאל, who agreed in only some cases. It is like אדמון himself in all seven rulings.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what he means: For the two rulings of חנן, the הלכה is like him and like the one who agrees with him. For the seven rulings of אדמון, the הלכה is not like the one who agrees with him. But like him, the הלכה is in all of them.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new reading of רבי זירא's statement that fits with the rule from Step 9.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'Not like the one who agrees with him' now means: don't limit yourself to רבן גמליאל, who agreed with אדמון in only some of the cases. Instead, follow אדמון himself in all seven of his rulings. This avoids the problem of Step 14, but the next step shows it goes too far for רבי יצחק בן אלעזר's rule.

keyTerms.meaning: Rather (introduces the corrected explanation)
But like him (pointing to what is still true)
In all of them

steps.whatToRemember: This is only a proposed reading. It says the הלכה follows אדמון in all seven rulings. Step 16 challenges it, and Steps 17–18 replace it.
steps.confusionAlert: In this proposed reading, 'אין הלכה כיוצא בו' does not mean we reject אדמון. It means we don't stop at the cases where רבן גמליאל agreed. But this reading is knocked down in Step 16.

phrases.english: Rather, this is what he means:
The two things that Chanan said
the halacha is like him and like the one who is similar to him,
the seven things that Admon said
the halacha is not like the one who is similar to him.
phrases.notes: Meaning: don't follow only רבן גמליאל, who agreed with אדמון in just some of the cases.

phrases.english: But like him, the halacha is in all of them.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the rejected reading from Step 14 with one that fits the rule from Step 9.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: 'אין הלכה כיוצא בו' means we reject אדמון and רבן גמליאל entirely.
steps.terutzMaskana: 'אין הלכה כיוצא בו' means we don't limit ourselves to רבן גמליאל's partial agreement. The הלכה follows אדמון in all seven rulings.

steps.title: The הלכה follows אדמון only where רבן גמליאל agreed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא attacks the reading from Step 15, that the הלכה follows אדמון in all seven rulings. רבי יצחק בן אלעזר said the הלכה follows אדמון only where רבן גמליאל said he agreed.
steps.simpleTranslation: But didn't רבי יצחק בן אלעזר say in the name of חזקיה: 'Anywhere רבן גמליאל said "I see the words of אדמון," the הלכה is like him'? So where he said it, yes. Where he did not say it, no!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the reading from Step 15. If the הלכה followed אדמון in all seven rulings, there would be no reason to limit it to the places where רבן גמליאל agreed.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יצחק בן אלעזר ties the הלכה to רבן גמליאל's words 'I see the words of אדמון.' The גמרא reads this precisely: where רבן גמליאל said it, the הלכה follows אדמון; where he did not, it does not. That clashes with the claim that אדמון wins in all seven rulings.

keyTerms.meaning: In the name of (quoting someone else)
'I see the words of אדמון', meaning רבן גמליאל agrees with אדמון
Yes
No

steps.confusionAlert: This is the same statement of רבי יצחק בן אלעזר used in Step 14. Here it is aimed at the new reading from Step 15, not the old one.

phrases.english: But didn't Rabbi Yitzchak ben Elazar say
in the name of Chizkiyya:
Anywhere that Rabban Gamliel said
"I see the words of Admon"
the halacha is like him.
Where he said it, yes;
where he did not say it, no!
phrases.notes: So in rulings where רבן גמליאל stayed quiet, the הלכה does not follow אדמון.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק בֶּן אֶלְעָזָר מִשְּׁמֵיהּ דְּחִזְקִיָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the reading of רבי זירא proposed in Step 15.
steps.kashyaTarget: The Step 15 reading that the הלכה follows אדמון in all seven rulings.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יצחק בן אלעזר limits the הלכה to the cases where רבן גמליאל agreed. The precise reading 'said, yes; did not say, no' rules out 'all seven.'

steps.title: New reading: Some of אדמון's rulings are the הלכה and some are not
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא rereads רבי זירא. The הלכה always follows חנן's two rulings. For אדמון's seven, the הלכה follows him in some and not in others.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, this is what he means: for the two rulings of חנן, the הלכה is like him and like the one who agrees with him. For the seven rulings of אדמון, some are cases where the הלכה is like him and like the one who agrees with him, and some are cases where the הלכה is not like him, but like the one who agrees with him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new reading of רבי זירא that fits רבי יצחק בן אלעזר's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The difference between חנן and אדמון is now this. חנן's two rulings are always the הלכה. אדמון's seven are split: some are the הלכה and some are not. The next line explains where the split falls.

keyTerms.meaning: This is what he means (the גמרא offers a new reading)
Like the one who agrees with him
Some of them

phrases.english: Rather, this is what he is saying:
phrases.notes: 'He' is רבי זירא, whose statement from Step 12 the גמרא is still trying to understand.

phrases.english: The two things that Chanan said:
the halacha is like him and like the one who agrees with him.
The seven things that Admon said:

phrases.aramaic: — יֵשׁ מֵהֶן שֶׁהֲלָכָה כְּמוֹתוֹ וְכַיּוֹצֵא בּוֹ,
phrases.english: in some of them the halacha is like him and like the one who agrees with him,
and in some of them the halacha is not like him,
but like the one who agrees with him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 16 by rereading רבי זירא.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי זירא meant that the הלכה follows אדמון in all seven rulings.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי זירא meant that אדמון's seven rulings are split. Only some of them are the הלכה, which fits רבי יצחק בן אלעזר.

steps.title: Where the split falls: wherever רבן גמליאל agreed
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא pins down which of אדמון's rulings are the הלכה: exactly the ones where רבן גמליאל said 'I see the words of אדמון.'
steps.simpleTranslation: Anywhere רבן גמליאל said 'I see the words of אדמון,' the הלכה is like him. In the others, no.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains the split from the last line by repeating רבי יצחק בן אלעזר's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The rule that was the challenge in Step 16 now becomes the explanation. Where רבן גמליאל spoke up in agreement, the הלכה follows אדמון. In the remaining rulings it does not.

keyTerms.meaning: The others (the remaining cases)

steps.whatToRemember: The two rulings of חנן are always the הלכה. Of the seven rulings of אדמון, only those where רבן גמליאל said 'I see the words of אדמון' are the הלכה.
steps.whyThisMatters: This gives a clear practical rule for deciding the הלכה in every argument of אדמון in this פרק.

phrases.english: Anywhere that Rabban Gamliel said
"I see the words of Admon"
the halacha is like him;
the others, no.
phrases.notes: 'The others' are אדמון's rulings where רבן גמליאל did not say he agreed.

steps.triggerLanguage: בְּכׇל מָקוֹם שֶׁאָמַר רַבָּן גַּמְלִיאֵל רוֹאֶה אֲנִי אֶת דִּבְרֵי אַדְמוֹן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Spells out which of אדמון's rulings fall on which side of the split from Step 17.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: The הלכה follows אדמון only in the rulings where רבן גמליאל said 'I see the words of אדמון.'

steps.title: New משנה: A man claims a field even though he signed as a witness on its sale
steps.stepSummary: A new משנה opens. Someone protests that a field is his, even though he signed as a witness on its sale. אדמון says his signature does not hurt his claim, because the new owner is easier to deal with than the old one.
steps.simpleTranslation: משנה: Someone protests that a field is his, and he is signed on its document as a witness. אדמון says: he can claim, 'The second one is easier for me, and the first is harder than him.'
steps.whatsHappening: A new משנה begins with another argument involving אדמון. This line gives the case and אדמון's opinion.
steps.deeperAnalysis: You might think that signing as a witness on the sale shows he agreed the field was not his. אדמון says no. He may have kept quiet against the tough seller and signed, so that the field would pass to an easier buyer he could later sue.

keyTerms.meaning: Our משנה (the start of a new משנה)
One who protests or contests a claim
Signed as a witness
Easier for me (to deal with)
Harder than him

phrases.english: MISHNA: One who contests ownership of a field,
and he is signed on it as a witness
phrases.notes: 'On it' means on the sale document for that field.

phrases.english: Admon says:
"The second is easier for me,"
phrases.notes: 'The second' is the buyer who now holds the field; 'the first' is the seller.

phrases.english: "and the first is harder than him."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new משנה. It is another of אדמון's rulings, so it connects to the discussion of when the הלכה follows him.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to אדמון, signing as a witness on the sale of a field does not cancel one's own claim to it. He can say the new owner is easier to sue than the old one.

steps.title: The חכמים say the signer lost his claim
steps.stepSummary: The חכמים disagree with אדמון. Once the man signed as a witness on the sale, he lost his right to claim the field.
steps.simpleTranslation: And the חכמים say: He lost his right.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה from Step 19 continues and gives the other side of the argument. The חכמים say the man who signed on the sale can no longer claim the field.
steps.deeperAnalysis: אדמון said the signature does not hurt the man, because the new owner may be easier to deal with. The חכמים say the opposite: by signing, he showed he agreed the field belonged to the seller. So his later claim is not accepted.

keyTerms.meaning: The Sages, the majority view in the משנה
He lost his right (to claim the field)

phrases.english: And the Sages say:
He lost his right.
phrases.notes: He means his right to claim the field, because his signature on the sale counts against him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the opposing view to אדמון's ruling in Step 19.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: According to the חכמים, a man who signs as a witness on the sale of a field loses his right to claim that field.

steps.title: Using the field as a boundary marker loses the claim
steps.stepSummary: Suppose the man used the field as a boundary marker for another field and described it as someone else's. Then he lost his claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: If he made it a marker for another field, he lost his right.
steps.whatsHappening: The משנה adds a second case. The man wrote a document about a different field and named this field as its border, calling it someone else's. In that case he lost his claim.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here the man himself described the field as belonging to another person. That is a stronger admission than just signing as a witness. So this case is treated more strictly, and the claim is lost.

keyTerms.meaning: He made it
A marker, here a boundary marker in a document
For another (field), or as belonging to another person

steps.confusionAlert: Don't mix this up with Step 20. There the man only signed as a witness, and אדמון and the חכמים argue about it. Here he himself described the field as someone else's, and he lost his claim.

phrases.english: If he made it a marker for another —
phrases.notes: He wrote a document about a different field and named this one as its border, calling it someone else's.

phrases.english: he lost his right.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds a second, stronger case after the argument over a witness's signature.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Someone who names a field as a boundary marker belonging to another person has lost his right to claim that field.
steps.whatToRemember: Signing as a witness: אדמון says the claim stays and the חכמים say it is lost. Naming the field as a border that belongs to someone else: the claim is lost.

steps.title: אביי: only a witness loses the claim, not a judge
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא opens with אביי. The משנה is talking only about a witness. A judge who certified the sale document does not lose his claim.
steps.simpleTranslation: גמרא: אביי said: They taught this only about a witness. But a judge did not lose his right.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins and sets a limit on the משנה. אביי says losing the claim applies to a witness who signed, not to a judge who signed to certify the document.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Both a witness and a judge put their signatures on documents, but the signatures do different jobs. אביי says only a witness's signature counts as agreeing to what the document says. The reason for this comes in the next step.

keyTerms.meaning: The discussion that explains the משנה
They taught this only about...
A witness
A judge, here one who signs to certify a document

phrases.english: Gemara
Abaye said:
They taught this only about a witness,

phrases.aramaic: אֲבָל דַּיָּין — לֹא אִיבֵּד אֶת זְכוּתוֹ.
phrases.english: but a judge did not lose his right.
phrases.notes: A judge here is someone who signed to confirm the document was valid, not someone who signed as a witness to the sale.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר אַבָּיֵי: לֹא שָׁנוּ אֶלָּא עֵד
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Opens the גמרא by limiting the משנה's ruling to a witness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Only a witness who signed on the sale loses his claim. A judge who certified the document keeps his claim.

steps.title: רבי חייא: witnesses read a document before signing
steps.stepSummary: אביי backs up his rule with a ברייתא of רבי חייא. Witnesses do not sign a document unless they have read it.
steps.simpleTranslation: As רבי חייא taught: Witnesses do not sign on a document unless they read it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source behind אביי's split. A witness must read the document first, so his signature shows he knew and accepted what it said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: A witness reads the whole document before signing, so he cannot say he didn't know it called the field the seller's. The ברייתא speaks only about witnesses. The point it implies is that a judge's signature does not show the same knowledge, so the judge keeps his claim.

keyTerms.meaning: A legal document
They read it

steps.whyThisMatters: This shows that the law treats a signature by how much the signer knew and accepted. It is not just about the ink on the page.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Chiya taught:
Witnesses do not sign on a document
unless they read it.
phrases.notes: So a witness surely knew what the document said about the field. Nothing is said here about judges reading it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the source and reason for אביי's distinction in Step 22.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's rule that a witness loses his claim but a judge does not.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The ברייתא of רבי חייא: witnesses sign only after reading the document, so a witness's signature shows he knew and accepted what it said.
